title: Worktops and surfaces — Sturij
description: Granite, marble, quartz and sintered stone on furniture built to carry it — templated, cut and fitted by a stone partner working to our drawing.

source.part: Part 6 — Worktops and surfaces (with Omega Stone, the partner of choice)

parts.heading: Stone, on furniture built to carry it.

standfirst.text: A worktop is the surface a kitchen lives on. We build the cabinetry to take the weight and the joints; a stone partner templates, cuts and fits the top once the furniture is in.

lines.text: Granite and marble are what they are — every slab different, the veining and colour formed in the ground, no two islands alike. Granite is hard-wearing and takes heat well; marble is softer and more beautiful, and asks to be looked after. We'll tell you honestly which suits how you cook.

An engineered stone: consistent from slab to slab, non-porous, and needs no sealing — the surface for a busy family kitchen where the look has to stay the same for years. Whites with soft veining, bold veins, plain solids.
The newer surfaces — very thin, very hard, stable in sunlight and under heat — for outdoor kitchens, cladding a media wall, or a run that has to take punishment.
The worktop is designed with the furniture, not after it: the island's overhang, the sink and hob cut-outs, the edge profile, a waterfall end, a matching upstand or splashback.
Once the cabinetry is fitted and level, the stone is templated to the room as it actually is, cut on the partner's machines, hand-finished at the edges and fitted by their own team.
Stone is heavy and unforgiving; it is fitted by the stone company that cut it, working to our drawing and to the room.
Ours is Omega Stone in Leeds.
Bring a sample of the stone you like to the design visit and we'll put it against the doors and the handles. It's the pairing that makes the room.

parts.heading: Cut in Leeds, fitted by the people who cut it.

standfirst.text: Our worktops and stone surfaces are templated, cut and fitted by Omega Stone — a Leeds stonemasonry with its own workshop, its own fitters and a showroom where you can see and touch the slab before you choose it.

lines.text: Omega Stone are specialists in granite, quartz, marble, porcelain and natural stone, based at their workshop in Pudsey, Leeds, with over fifteen years' experience, their own expert fitters and CNC machinery, and membership of the Worktop Fabricators Federation. They supply and fit for homes and businesses across Yorkshire and beyond — Harrogate, Wetherby and York are on their own list.

A wider choice of stone than we could ever hold ourselves: quartz from Silestone by Cosentino, Caesarstone, Cambria, Compac, CRL, Quartzforms and more, in the popular styles — Carrara whites, Calacatta and Statuario veining, greys, golds; granite from Levantina, Sensa by Cosentino and other suppliers — every slab unique; sintered stone and porcelain — Dekton, Neolith, Lapitec, CRL Ceralsio — for outdoor kitchens, thin profiles and hard-wearing surfaces; terrazzo; and stone beyond the kitchen — media walls, backlit slabs, hearths, cladding and staircases — which is why a Sturij media wall can carry a stone face or a stone hearth from the same partner.

You can choose your slab at their Leeds showroom. Once our cabinetry is fitted and level, they template to the room, cut in their workshop, and fit — their site says three to seven days from template, and three to four hours to fit an average kitchen. Most slabs run to 3.2 m by 1.6 m; four of their quartz colours come as "super jumbo" slabs at 3.5 m by 2 m for a long run with fewer joins. Their quartz is guaranteed against staining and needs no sealing; payment for the stone is taken after template, before cutting, because a cut slab fits only your room.
Omega Stone publish their guarantees, their cleaning and maintenance guidance and their environmental policy on their own site; we'll point you to them with your quote.
We design the top with the furniture; they make it real. If you want to see the stone first, we'll book you into their showroom.

faq.q: Granite, quartz or sintered — which should I choose?

a.text: Depends on how you cook and what you want to see. Granite for character and heat; quartz for consistency and no maintenance; sintered stone for outdoor, ultra-thin or heavy-use surfaces. We'll show you samples against your doors at the design visit.
Granite and marble do, periodically; quartz doesn't. We'll tell you what your surface needs and how often.
On a long run, yes — slabs have a maximum size. Joins are planned on the drawing where they'll be least visible, and finished tight.

faq.q: Can I have a waterfall end or a stone splashback?

a.text: Yes — both are drawn with the furniture and cut from the same slab where the pattern needs to flow.
After the cabinetry is in and level. The stone is templated to the fitted furniture, then cut and fitted — there's a gap between the two visits, which we'll give you at the design stage.

faq.q: Can I see the actual slab?

a.text: For natural stone, yes — every slab is different, and you can choose yours at the yard.

faq.q: Do you do the stone yourselves?

a.text: No. We make the furniture; a specialist stone company templates, cuts and fits the surface, working to our drawing. It's the right way round — each does the part it does best.
